predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Toledo and its district, a governorship of the Caliphate of Córdoba until 'In 1018, Ismail expelled the governor of the city of Toledo'

successors.name: Kingdom of Castile
successors.text: the taifa's last shape (the Toledan lands, Valencia having slipped away); infobox 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Toledo (Crown of Castile)'; 'Toledo officially and peacefully fell into Christian hands on…

ledger.x: 1018: Toledo breaks away from the Caliphate of Córdoba.
1062: Ferdinand I invades the east of Toledo's taifa.
1075: Toledo conquers the taifa of Córdoba.
1085: Valencia is no longer held from Toledo.

wars.name: Ferdinand I's invasion of the taifa of Toledo
wars.outcome: Ferdinand took Talamanca, besieged Alcalá de Henares and left when al-Ma'mun agreed to pay parias.

wars.name: Toledan annexation of Valencia
wars.outcome: Al-Ma'mun seized Valencia and installed his vizier as governor; Ferdinand I's own siege of Valencia in 1065 failed ('did not have the forces to take the city').

wars.name: Toledo and Seville over Córdoba
wars.outcome: Seville took Córdoba in 1070 after defeating the Toledan army; Toledo held the Cordoban lands 1075-1077; Seville regained them by 1078.

wars.name: Conquest of Toledo
wars.outcome: Toledo surrendered to Alfonso VI in May 1085 and became the Kingdom of Toledo within Castile; al-Qadir was sent to Valencia.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given for any frontier of the taifa; the Castilian frontier was approximate, and the pages date no boundary except the places named in 1062.

sources.title: Alfonso VI of León and Castile
